title: The art of looking slower
excerpt: Why the best photographs appear when you stop searching for them.
body: Sometimes you need to put the camera down and simply look. Light settles on branches, the air shifts, and the urge to hurry fades. This is where attentive photography begins.
Choose one place and spend half an hour there. Instead of searching for the perfect subject, watch the light. The same landscape can tell many different stories.

title: The light already around us
excerpt: A window, an overcast day, and a little trust — the ingredients for a living portrait.
body: Natural light lets you start a session with a simple setup. A large window becomes a soft light source, and a neutral wall makes a quiet backdrop.
Leave space for movement and conversation. A small pause often reveals more than a carefully planned pose.

title: Mountain notes: closer to the sky
excerpt: A few thoughts on the road, scale, and being small in a wide world.
body: In the mountains, you feel the scale of things. The journey slows down, and familiar details matter: a trail, a cloud, a strip of light across a slope.
A series needs more than one striking photograph. Details and pauses between wide views help convey the feeling of a journey.
